title: Agent Usage: every Agent dispatch
description: One row per returned Agent dispatch, of any agent type: the marketplace's defined agents, built-ins (Explore, general-purpose, Plan) and other plugins' agents (completed or errored; a denied dispatch writes none), written by the agent-watcher mod when the agent returns. A pr-review or pr-team dispatch (reviewer, fixer, orchestrator, planner, closer) belongs to its run; any other dispatch is a generic row whose skill, role, run id, agent id and PR come from its prompt's leading header block (`SKILL:`, `AGENT_ROLE:`, `RUN_ID:`, `AGENT_ID:`, `PR:`), falling back to `standalone`, `other`, a generated run id, the type's name and null; the other header keys land in `fields`. Records who ran (role, subagent_type, model), its cost (tokens, context_tokens, requests, tool_uses, duration_s) and, for fixer and closer rows, outcome counts. Loaded line-by-line as JSONL/NDJSON: each line of the data file is one complete object matching this schema.

logged_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC time the row was built.

run_id.description: The dispatch's RUN_ID (`pr<N>_<UTC yyyymmddTHHMMSSZ>` for pr-review and pr-team); groups the rows of one run. A generic dispatch logs its header RUN_ID, or, when it names none or the value holds a path separator, its own `standalone_<UTC yyyymmddTHHMMSSZ>_<seq>`. Never holds a path separator.

pr.description: PR number under review, not zero-padded; null when the run names none. A generic row takes its header `PR:` value when it is a positive integer.

skill.description: The skill that dispatched the run: `pr-review` or `pr-team` for their runs; for any other dispatch the header `SKILL:` value with a leading `<plugin>:` stripped, else `standalone` (no `SKILL:` line, or a value off the pattern); for a forked skill (`context: fork`, from agent-watcher 0.8.0 on) the skill's own name, read the same way.

role.description: The tracked role: `reviewer`, `fixer`, `orchestrator`, `planner` or `closer` in a pr-review or pr-team run (a roast is a reviewer; `subagent_type` or `agent_id` tells it apart). A generic row takes its header `AGENT_ROLE:` value, else `other` (no line, a value off the pattern, or `fixer` / `closer`, whose counts only a layer computes).

agent_id.description: Slot id from the dispatch plan, or `orchestrator_plan` / `orchestrator_consolidate` / `fixer_plan` / `closer`. A generic row: its header `AGENT_ID:` value, else the agent type's name without its plugin prefix (`messenger`; `general-purpose` when the call names no type). Never holds a path separator.

subagent_type.description: The Agent call's `subagent_type`; null when the call named none.

model.description: Full model id: the engine-resolved model, else the requested one; null when neither is known.

model_family.description: The family token found in `model`; `unknown` when it holds none (or `model` is null).

tokens.description: Input + output + cache read + cache creation tokens summed over every model request the agent made, as the engine reports each: what the run billed. 0 when unmeasured. Rows written before agent-watcher 0.7.0 hold, for a foreground dispatch, the last request's count instead (what `context_tokens` now holds). A row without the `context_tokens` key predates 0.7.0.

context_tokens.description: The same four counts for the agent's last model request that reported usage, alone: its context size at the end, the figure its completion notification shows. Null when unknown (an errored result, a foreground result without a total, or an agent none of whose requests reported usage). Every row from agent-watcher 0.7.0 on carries it; older rows lack it.

requests.description: Model requests the agent's loop made, whether or not a response with usage came back. Tool calls happen between requests, and one request may ask for several, so this is not `tool_uses`. Null when no request was heard (an errored result, or an agent none of whose requests the watcher heard). Every row from agent-watcher 0.7.0 on carries it; older rows lack it.

signal.description: The return block's SIGNAL, cut to 200 characters; `NO_BLOCK` when the agent returned without a return block; `ERROR` for an errored Agent result; `UNRECOGNIZED` when the SIGNAL value holds a path separator, so no path enters the log.

notes.description: `agent-watcher auto row; <role> <signal>`, plus `; usage not measured` when the engine reported no usage, or `; usage not measured; agent errored` for an errored result. Never holds a path separator.

fields.description: Generic rows only, absent when empty: the leading header block's keys the watcher did not consume, plus any consumed value that fell back, each value as written (trimmed). A value holding a path separator is dropped with its key, so no local or absolute path enters the log; any other value is cut to 200 characters.

issues_assigned.description: Fixer and closer rows only. Number of issues the fixer was assigned (pr-review: the length of its `issue_ids` in the run's waves.json; pr-team: always null, the block carries no assignment); null when unknown.

issues_fixed.description: Fixer and closer rows only. Issues fixed (pr-review: the report's `fixed`; pr-team: the block's FIXED ids); null when unknown.

issues_bubbled.description: Fixer and closer rows only. Issues bubbled (pr-review: the report's `bubbled`; pr-team: the block's BUBBLED ids); null when unknown.

files_touched.description: Fixer and closer rows only. Distinct files edited (pr-review: `files` across the report's `fixed` entries; pr-team: the block's EDITED count); null when unknown.

then.description: Fixer and closer rows carry the four outcome counts (null when unknown).

else.description: Every other role carries none of the outcome counts.
